The last three weeks of class is dedicated to in-class workshops in which students go through the research process, which includes skills such as identifying the topic, identifying the question, narrowing down the question, identifying relevant sources, strategically reading the identified sources by applying reading strategies, outlining the paper, and drafting the paper. 
In-class workshops help limits AI in several ways. First, students are given sufficient time to go through and enjoy the research process and as a result of not being rushed, they are not tempted to use AI. Second, students work in class, which helps keep them accountable in the learning process. Last but not least, students know that their professor emphasizes the process over the final product, so they are more invested in engaging with the process as opposed to producing a flawless final product.
